headline: GOLD CLAWS BACK TO $4,145 THURSDAY MORNING — PRECIOUS METALS RECOUP GROUND AFTER CPI-DRIVEN SELLOFF
snippet: Spot gold recovered to $4,145–$4,147/oz Thursday morning after closing at $4,104 on Wednesday following the September CPI shock that drove a 6% single-day drop in silver. The rebound signals short-term technical support; all eyes now on the October 27–28 FOMC meeting as the next major catalyst.

headline: LUCA MINING RAISES C$211M TO CLOSE COZAMIN COPPER-SILVER DEAL — CAPSTONE PURCHASE CLEARS FINAL FUNDING HURDLE
snippet: Luca Mining completed C$211M in subscription receipt financings for its proposed purchase of Capstone Copper's producing Cozamin mine in Mexico, clearing the final funding hurdle. Total consideration is $290M upfront plus up to $95M deferred and contingent; the deal is now expected to close imminently.

headline: SSR MINING ACQUIRES ROXMORE RESOURCES FOR $712M — CONVERSE GOLD PROJECT SITS 6KM FROM MARIGOLD MINE
snippet: SSR Mining agreed to acquire Roxmore Resources and its Converse gold project in Nevada for approximately $712M total value, with in-the-money diluted equity at $464M and enterprise value at $392M. Converse sits six kilometres from SSR's Marigold complex, offering clear operational synergies in a tier-1 jurisdiction.

headline: CODELCO SUSPENDS EL TENIENTE AFTER FATAL LANDSLIDE — BHP ESCONDIDA AVERTS STRIKE WITH PRELIMINARY DEAL
snippet: Codelco partially suspended operations at its El Teniente copper mine following a fatal landslide, while BHP reached a preliminary agreement to avert a threatened strike at Escondida — the world's largest copper mine. The dual supply disruptions are providing a floor under copper prices near $6.53/lb despite macro headwinds from the CPI surprise.

headline: MORE THAN A DOZEN US FIRMS EYE MALAYSIA RARE EARTHS — PUSH TO BREAK CHINA'S PROCESSING STRANGLEHOLD ACCELERATES
snippet: More than a dozen US companies are actively exploring opportunities in Malaysia's rare earths industry as a hedge against China's ongoing export licence restrictions. The push intensifies ahead of DFARS defence sourcing rules taking effect January 1, 2027, which will require US defence contractors to source critical minerals outside China.

headline: NEW MEXICO CLOSES DOOR ON URANIUM LEASES ON STATE TRUST LAND — OPERATORS INSIDE FAST-41 PROGRAM HOLD THEIR STATUS
snippet: New Mexico's Land Commissioner signed an executive order banning new uranium mining leases on state trust lands, effective September 4, 2026. Projects already enrolled in the federal FAST-41 expedited permitting program retain their permits, limiting the practical impact — but the order signals hardening political headwinds for in-situ recovery developers in the state.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM PRICE HITS RECORD US$96/LB — Q3 DATA CONFIRMS STRUCTURAL TIGHTENING AS REACTORS RAMP
snippet: Uranium's long-term contract price reached a new record of US$96/lb in Q3 2026 as global nuclear energy demand continues to outpace supply additions. The milestone reinforces the bull case for uranium developers, even as many junior uranium equities remain under pressure from broader risk-off sentiment.

headline: GREENLAND MINES JUMPS ON US-DENMARK-GREENLAND SECURITY PACT — SARFARTOQ RARE EARTH ACREAGE DRAWS STRATEGIC INTEREST
snippet: Shares of Greenland Mines (GRML) surged after a US-Denmark-Greenland security agreement spotlighted the territory's critical minerals potential. The company's Sarfartoq rare earth project is among the assets drawing US strategic interest, as the Western world accelerates non-Chinese rare earth supply chain development.

headline: COPPER EYES RECORD HIGHS DESPITE RATE FEAR PAUSE — ANALYSTS SEE STRUCTURAL DEFICIT OVERRIDING MACRO NOISE
snippet: Despite a CPI-driven pullback, analysts at multiple firms argue that copper's structural supply deficit and improving demand signals from China make a sustained run toward the September 9 settlement record of $6.89/lb achievable. Supply disruptions at El Teniente and the near-miss at Escondida underscore how exposed the market is to any further production outages.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE AND SPODUMENE EACH DOWN 25% IN A MONTH — SECTOR WAITS FOR DEMAND SIGNAL BEFORE RE-RATING
snippet: Spot lithium carbonate and spodumene prices have each shed approximately 25% over the past month, with the metal falling more than a fifth in September alone. Analysts remain constructive on long-term fundamentals but say the market needs a clear demand inflection from Chinese battery makers before any durable re-rating of junior lithium equities.
